question: Should OpenClaw adopt the proposed core-level durable authority, public durable.* configuration, and shared-SQLite recovery contract, or keep recovery within existing owner-specific paths?
rationale: The patch is a substantial new product and persistence boundary rather than a repair to an established contract; automated review cannot choose whether that permanent core surface should exist.

options.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
options.body: Accept the owner-first durable boundary, then require a current-main rebase and explicit fresh-install and upgrade proof before merging.

options.title: Keep recovery owner-specific
options.body: Decline the shared durable authority and retain or improve recovery through task, flow, subagent, and session owners without a new core runtime layer.

options.title: Pause pending RFC decision
options.body: Leave this implementation unmerged until the linked RFC records the maintainer-approved scope and ownership boundary.

recommendation.title: Sponsor a narrowed core contract
recommendation.body: Accept the owner-first durable boundary, then require a current-main rebase and explicit fresh-install and upgrade proof before merging.

likelyOwner.reason: This contributor has the strongest available history for explaining the proposed durable boundary and its implementation; upstream sponsorship remains a maintainer decision.
